page.layout: One printed page (right page of the opening; the left strip is the edge of the neighbouring page and is not transcribed). Running head at top centre with page number at top right. Main text in one column, with printed line numbers 5 to 35 in the left margin. No notes in the right margin. Under the text: signature at left and catchword at right.

main_text.p: mere evidenter, obsignare conferendo, claudere signo appofito. Caeterum signum est vel γνώρισμα[?], indicium, ein Kenn vnd Merckzeichen / vel μνημόσυνον, memoriale, ein Denckzeichen; vel σφραγίς, Sigillum. Rursus signum 5est vel ἐνδεικτικὸν[?], rei praesentis; vel μνημόσυνον, rei praeteritae; vel προγνωστικὸν[?], rei futurae. Exempla plurima occurrunt in sacris. Iris est signum gratiae Dei Gen.9.Circumcisio est signum & sigillum foederis gratiae Gen.17. verf.11. Rom.4. verf.11. Pascha est memoriale (seu monumentum 10transitus Exod.12. v.13. Praecepta Dei alligata manibus Israelitarum erant signum & typus accuratae & perpetuae observationis. Deut.6. v.8. Ionas in ventre ceti fuit signum filij hominis commoraturi in ventre terrae. Matth.16. v.4. rubedo caeli est prognosticum tempestatis. ibid. v.2. cere-15moniae V.T. erant typi Christi. epist. ad Hebr. passim. sacra-menta sunt signa donantia, sive pingentia & significantia; obsignantia, sive certificantia; denique applicantia, sive praebentia & exhibentia ipsum signatum in legitimo usu. 1. Cor.11. verf.24.25. Signatum est, quod a signo repraesentatur, nempe significando, obsignando, vel exhi-bendo.

LII Explicatis transcendentibus restant praedicamenta, quae sunt summa entis genera, 25numero decem. Quintilianus scite ait: Aristoteles decem elementa constituit, circa quae versari videatur omnis quaestio. Et Melanchthon praedicamenta eleganter vocat classes seu series rerum omnium. Est enim praedicamentum locus, quo omneens, sive omnis conceptus simplex realis, refertur 30ad poteft, hoc ordine: substantia, quantitas, qualitas, actio, passio, relatio, quando, ubi, situs, habitus.

LIII. Praedicamentum aliud est substantiae, aliud accidentis. Nam species entis sunt duae, substantia & accidens. Substantia est ens per se subsistens, hoc est, 35non indigens subiecto inhaesionis, seu, non inhaerens alij: ut Deus, Spiritus creatus, & corpus. Gen. 1. & 2. Heb. 1.

page.notes: Printed line numbers 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30 and 35 stand in the left margin and are given as notes at their lines. Doubtful Greek: γνώρισμα, ἐνδεικτικὸν and προγνωστικὸν are read from a small, blurred scan and are marked [?]. The word "poteft" at line 30 is a printed line break; "ad" in the first line of the second paragraph is part of the printed "hoc ordine" sentence, and the reading "ad poteft" is uncertain. The catchword "verf.14." sits at the right foot after "Heb. 1."; the first paragraph continues from the previous page.
